name: Matrix-Game 3.5
tagline: Causal DiT with 3D re-projected patch memory
summary: Matrix-Game 3.5 distills a bidirectional world model into a few-step fully causal generator and keeps long-term memory as geometry: historical VAE-latent patches are lifted to 3D with metric depth, re-projected into the target view and inserted as tokens of one pose-aware sequence. Each 3-latent-frame chunk attends causally to a clean anchor, the preceding chunks, one chunk-local context frame and its patch memory; third-person models add multi-view reference tokens for the controlled character. Camera pose enters through tiled PRoPE with no new parameters. A 3-step causal student reaches up to 20 fps at 1280x704 on one H100 with INT8, GPU retrieval and a 75%-pruned decoder (company claim).
facts: Wan2.2 VAE 4x16x16 → 44x80x48 latent per latent frame at 1280x704; 2x2 patchify (Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config) → 22x40 = 880 tokens per latent frame, 2,640 per 3-latent chunk of 12 frames [D]; 48 latent channels

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT: 30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 (HF config); the full DiT is fine-tuned with the text encoder and VAE frozen; the only learnable additions are the reference-token embeddings

Block-causal chunks of 3 latent frames: the chunk's 2,640 queries attend to a rolling KV window (clean anchor + ≤6 previous chunks = ≤19 latent frames, released config), 1 chunk-local context frame, 3 frames of patch memory (≤1 token per target cell) and itself: ≤26 latent frames ≈ 22,880 K/V tokens per chunk [D]; causal training window 1 anchor + 7 chunks = 22 positions; the paper's ≈2.3x sequence bound is for the bidirectional base model's 21-frame sample

Camera pose via tiled PRoPE in every block: after RoPE, queries × Pᵀ, keys and values × P⁻¹, outputs × P, tiled over all head channels, no new parameters; translations recentred on the first target frame and log-compressed

Perceptual flow matching causal adaptation (10k steps), then curriculum self-rollout DMD (1,000 outer steps, 5:1 update ratio) → 3-step causal generator; prefix and chunk-local context held at the next noise level each substep (HiAR), anchor clean
MG-LightVAE, 75%-pruned Wan2.2 decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 1280x704; 'VAE decoding becomes the primary latency bottleneck' once the DiT is accelerated

Patch memory (MosaicMem-style): patches lifted to 3D with metric depth and poses, frustum-queried, z-buffered and scattered into a target-aligned memory frame; retrieval runs for every generated chunk (on GPU, inside the real-time loop), and each chunk is decoded and registered before the next query; only the dynamic-object filter runs once per segment, outside the denoising loop; the memory bank grows with rollout length, the per-chunk sequence does not

Up to 20 output frames/s at 1280x704, batch 1, one H100, including the INT8 3-step DiT, online retrieval and MG-LightVAE decode (company claim; the VLM prompt rewriter runs asynchronously); undistilled model in the SANA-WM benchmark: 10.9 one-minute videos/hour at 77.0 GB peak, #G = 1, measured on an 8xH100 node (authors' Table 1)

Long-term memory is geometric (patch memory); short-term context is a bounded rolling KV window (anchor + ≤6 chunks), so per-chunk DiT cost stops growing once the window fills [D]; memory retrieval runs every chunk on the real-time path, and only the dynamic-object filter is amortised per segment

name: Cosmos 3
tagline: Reasoner and generator towers share one attention
summary: An omnimodal world model built as a mixture of transformers: a reasoner tower (initialized from Qwen3-VL, then further pre-trained and fine-tuned) runs autoregressively over text and ViT tokens, and a generator tower denoises video latents, audio and action tokens with flow matching. The towers keep their own norms, attention projections and MLPs but share one self-attention operator, so every diffusion token can read the AR context. One set of weights serves generation, forward and inverse dynamics and a policy, selected by which tokens are clean and which are noisy; the post-trained DROID policy runs 4 steps with CFG split across 2 RTX Pro 6000 GPUs and skips video decoding.
facts: Generation: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B VAE latents, 4x temporal and 32x32 spatial (16x16 VAE + 2x2 patch merge), linearly projected to the hidden size, so ⌈H/32⌉ x ⌈W/32⌉ tokens per latent frame, e.g. 23 x 40 = 920 at 720p 16:9, because an odd latent side is zero-padded before the merge [D]; understanding: ViT tokens (patch 16, 2x2 merge); audio 25 tokens/s (48 kHz, hop 1920)

Nano: 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads / 8 KV heads of 128, FFN 12,288 in each of two towers = 16B (from Qwen3-VL-8B); Super: 64 layers, hidden 5120, 64 / 8 heads, FFN 25,600 = 64B; Edge 4B (28 layers, hidden 2048) released 20 Jul 2026

Shared self-attention: AR tokens attend causally to AR tokens only; DM tokens attend bidirectionally over all AR + DM tokens; AR tokens never read DM tokens; training packs a fixed 74,000-token context

Action vectors (relative ego pose 9-D, effector pose 9-D, grasp state; 10-D single arm up to 57-D egocentric human) enter as DM tokens through per-embodiment input and output projections; the MoT backbone is shared; the DROID policy re-initializes the action encoder, decoding MLP and action embedding tokens

Flow matching: 50 steps for generation (guidance 6, shift 10), 4 steps for the DROID policy (guidance 3, shift 5) predicting 32 absolute joint-position actions at 15 Hz; the reasoner pass is computed once and cached across all steps; σ enters as a sinusoidal timestep embedding (256 → Linear-SiLU-Linear) added to every noisy video, audio and action token after its input projection, with no AdaLN in the layers (code)
Wan2.2 VAE decoder for video; skipped in policy serving, where only the action tokens are read

The report describes no streaming rollout; the Nano model card chains 16-frame forward-dynamics chunks, each re-conditioned on the previous chunk's last generated frame. Within each sample the generator attends bidirectionally over its AR + DM tokens; paged KV caching only for reasoner serving (TensorRT-LLM / vLLM)

Nano 720p text-to-video on one GPU: 297 s on H100 NVL vs 115 s on B200 (PyTorch; frames and steps not stated); policy served on 2 RTX Pro 6000 with CFG parallelism, per-chunk latency not disclosed (company claims)

Each token passes through one tower, so per-token compute stays near the dense 8B backbone while total parameters grow ≈1.8x (15.75B vs 8.77B) [D]; the DROID policy runs 4 steps x a 540x640 three-view canvas and skips decoding the video latents

name: SANA-WM
tagline: Hybrid linear DiT with a fixed-size state
summary: A minute-scale camera-controlled world model whose DiT replaces most softmax attention with frame-wise Gated DeltaNet: 15 of 20 blocks keep a D×D recurrent state per head, updated once per latent frame, and only 5 blocks use softmax attention, run at deployment with an attention sink plus a local window. The LTX2 VAE packs 8 raw frames into one 128-channel latent frame, so 60 s of 720p fits one GPU. Self Forcing distillation gives a 4-step chunk-causal generator; with NVFP4 on one RTX 5090 it denoises 60 s of 720p in 34 s (authors).
facts: LTX2 VAE, 128 latent channels, one latent frame per 8 raw frames; spatial stride and tokens per latent frame at 720p are not stated in the paper, which calls the representation 8x smaller than Wan2.1-VAE's

Hybrid linear DiT from SANA-Video: 20 blocks, d 2240, 20 heads of 112; 15 frame-wise Gated DeltaNet blocks + softmax attention at layers {3, 7, 11, 15, 19}, keeping the original QKV and output projections; text, video and pose tokens pass through the alternating blocks; LayerNorm (no affine) + adaLN-single shift/scale/gate on the attention and FFN sub-layers, cross-attention without norm (released code)

GDN blocks: a D×D recurrent state per head updated once per latent frame from all S spatial tokens (forward scan global, reversed scan reset at chunk boundaries in the chunk-causal variant); softmax blocks: first latent frame as sink + local temporal window at deployment; chunk = 3 latent frames (first chunk 4), deployment window = sink + 2 cached chunks (released config and CLI)

6-DoF camera trajectory only (the CLI's WASD/IJKL keys are rolled out to a trajectory): UCPE relative camera encoding on the geometric channels of a camera attention branch at latent-frame rate, plus the 8 raw-frame Plücker raymaps of one VAE stride packed into a 48-channel tensor through a zero-initialized 3D patch embedder; applied in every block
Flow matching; 60-step chunk-causal AR generator distilled with Self Forcing to 4 steps; bidirectional, chunk-causal and distilled variants each run on one GPU
LTX2 VAE decoder → 720p at 16 fps (961 frames = 60 s [D]); optional second stage: LTX-2 17B refiner with a rank-384 LoRA, 3 Euler steps

15 GDN layers each hold a main and a camera-branch D×D state per head plus a D-vector normalizer: 2 × 20 × 112² + 20 × 112 = 504,000 fp32 values ≈ 2.0 MB per layer, ≈30 MB for all 15 [D]; the 5 softmax layers keep a sink + window KV, so memory is constant in rollout length (all-softmax runs out of memory at 60 s on an H100, Fig. 7b); no explicit 3D scene memory

60 s of 720p: DiT time on one H100 21.7 min at 60 steps → 43 s at 4 steps → 29 s with the sink (34 s end to end); 34 s DiT on one RTX 5090 with NVFP4, 42 s with the 7.3 s VAE decode (authors, Fig. 7a); 433 ms per denoising step at 720p on one H100, 5.68 GiB (Table 3, 5 s clips); 24.1 one-minute videos per hour on 8 H100s (Table 2)

At deployment, per-chunk cost is constant in rollout length in all 20 layers (GDN state in 15, sink + local-window KV in 5); the VAE swap is the bigger lever per step (3.4x latency, 8.9 → 5.4 GiB, while also going from 480p to 720p); replacing cumulative linear attention with hybrid GDN + softmax costs 1.17x per step (433.2 vs 371.7 ms) and raises memory from 5.40 to 5.68 GiB [D]

name: Matrix-Game 3.0
tagline: Bidirectional segment DiT with retrieved memory
summary: Skywork's 720p successor to Matrix-Game 2.0, built on Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. Unlike its predecessor it keeps a bidirectional DiT: each streaming segment denoises 10 new latent frames jointly with 4 past latents and 5 memory latents retrieved by camera pose and frustum overlap, all in one self-attention sequence with no KV cache. Multi-segment DMD distils it to 3 steps. The reported ~40 FPS at 720p needs 8 GPUs for the DiT plus 1 for the VAE, INT8 attention projections, a 75%-pruned decoder and GPU-side retrieval (company claim).
facts: Wan2.2 VAE (4x16x16) + 1x2x2 patchify; a 704x1280 frame becomes a 44x80 latent and a 22x40 grid of 880 tokens per latent frame [D]; one latent frame = 4 video frames (the first latent holds 1); 10 latent frames per segment = 40 video frames (first segment 57)

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 per the HF config); action modules in the first 15 blocks as in Matrix-Game 2.0; teacher and student share one bidirectional architecture; a 28B MoE scale-up is also trained

Bidirectional within a segment: 5 retrieved memory latents + 4 past latents + 10 noisy current latents in one sequence (first segment: reference latent + 14 noisy latents), ≈16,720 tokens per segment [D]; head-wise perturbed RoPE bases; no KV cache

Keyboard actions through a dedicated cross-attention module, mouse signals through self-attention (Matrix-Game 2.0 design), in blocks 1-15; relative Plücker cues encode the camera geometry between the target and the retrieved memory; in every block a Plücker-driven scale/shift (four 3072x3072 layers per block; camera layers total ≈1.17B params in the checkpoint [D]) modulates the tokens after self-attention
Flow matching; multi-segment self-rollout DMD (1-6 segments, memory from an online pool) → 3 distilled steps per segment; error collection and injection train the model on its own imperfect histories
MG-LightVAE: Wan2.2 decoder with reduced hidden widths (LightX2V-style), 50% or 75% pruned; decode 0.76 → 0.30 → 0.13 s per 17-frame 720x1280 clip (PSNR 33.79 → 31.84 → 31.14 dB); runs on its own GPU

Camera-aware retrieval: each query view takes the past frame with the highest frustum-overlap score (exact on CPU, approximate on GPU); the first latent can be kept as a persistent sink; without a KV cache the memory and past tokens are re-processed at every step

~40 FPS at 720p on an asynchronous 8+1 pipeline (8 DiT GPUs + 1 VAE GPU); GPU model not named (results cover H-series with FlashAttention 3 and A-series with FlashAttention 2); leave-one-out Table 1: 27.38 FPS without INT8, 25.79 without MG-LightVAE, 6.60 with CPU retrieval; single-node 7+1 'slightly lower' (company claim); 3.1 one-minute videos/hour on 8 H100s in SANA-WM's benchmark (third party; Matrix-Game 3.0's multi-step, undistilled AR setting, not the 3-step real-time pipeline); the ~40 FPS figure is a company claim

Real time is a systems result: 9 GPUs, INT8 on the attention projections only (+46% [D]), a decoder the authors report as up to 5.2x faster (Table 2 decode times imply ≈5.8x [D]) (+55% [D]) and GPU retrieval (≈6.1x [D]); the authors say VAE decode is the bottleneck once the DiT is optimized

name: LeWorldModel (LeWM)
tagline: One token per frame, CEM plans in under a second
summary: The smallest JEPA world model in the gallery: a ViT-Tiny encoder and a 6-layer predictor trained end to end from pixels with two losses only (next-embedding MSE plus the SIGReg Gaussian regularizer), with no EMA, stop-gradient or frozen foundation encoder. Each frame is squeezed into a single 192-d [CLS] embedding, so the predictor sees at most 3 tokens, and a CEM plan of 300 samples x up to 30 iterations x horizon 5 finishes in 0.98 s against 47 s for DINO-WM.
facts: One 192-d token per 224x224 frame: the last-layer [CLS] embedding of a ViT-Tiny (patch 14, 12 layers, 3 heads, width 192, ~5M) followed by a 1-layer MLP projector with BatchNorm
Predictor: 6 layers, d 192, 16 heads of 64, MLP 2048, dropout 0.1, learned positional embeddings; ~10M; followed by a projector of the same design as the encoder's
Temporal causal mask over the history of frame embeddings; N = 3 frames (paper: 1 for TwoRoom; the released TwoRoom checkpoint and code use 3), i.e. at most 3 tokens per predictor call [D]
Zero-initialised AdaLN at every predictor layer; with frameskip 5 the 5 actions between frames form one 10-d action block, embedded to width 192
One pass regresses the next frame embedding (MSE); encoder and predictor trained jointly, SIGReg keeps the embeddings Gaussian to prevent collapse
None in training or planning; a diagnostic cross-attention decoder (196 queries → 224x224) only visualizes what the latent retains
Window of N = 3 frame embeddings; no KV cache

Full plan 0.98 s vs 47 s for DINO-WM, averaged over 50 runs (authors; GPU not stated); CEM with 300 samples, top 30, up to 30 iterations (PushT) or 10, horizon 5 latent steps = 25 environment steps, whole plan executed before replanning

196x fewer tokens per frame than DINO-WM [D]; a PushT plan is 150 sequential batched calls (30 iterations x 5 predictor steps), each over 300 candidates with windows of 1, 2, 3, 3, 3 tokens: ~7-21 GFLOP per call, ~2.5 TFLOP per plan [D], a latency-bound chain rather than a throughput job

name: Fast-WAM
tagline: Video DiT plus action expert, no imagined video
summary: A mixture-of-transformers world-action model that keeps video co-training but drops test-time imagination. A Wan2.2-5B video DiT and a 1B action-expert DiT (the same architecture at d 1024) share attention; in training, future video latents and the action chunk are denoised jointly under a structured mask, while at inference the video DiT runs once over the clean first-frame tokens and the action expert denoises a 32-step chunk in 10 steps. That gives 190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D against 810 ms for the Fast-WAM-IDM variant.
facts: Wan2.2 VAE latents of the observation, with the multi-camera images concatenated into one image; training video chunks of 9 frames after 4x temporal downsampling; 98 tokens per latent frame on LIBERO (224x448 input) and 120 on RoboTwin (384x320) [D from released config]; a proprioceptive-state token joins the T5 context (code)

Video DiT from Wan2.2-5B (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14,336 per its config.json) plus an action expert with the same architecture at d 1024 (1B); T5 text reaches all tokens through cross-attention; norms and timestep modulation not detailed in the paper

Shared attention with a structured mask: clean first-frame tokens attend to nothing else; future video tokens (training only) attend within the video branch and to the first frame; action tokens attend within the action branch and to the first frame, never to future video
Action chunk of h = 32 as tokens in the action expert, denoised by flow matching; at inference the expert reads the single-pass video features through the shared attention

Training: joint flow matching over actions and future video latents (paper: logit-normal t; released code: shift-warped uniform t with a bell-shaped loss weight); inference: one video-DiT pass over the clean first frame, then 10 action denoising steps at CFG 1.0 (no second pass)
None at deployment: no future video tokens are instantiated, denoised or decoded

Single-chunk policy; the outer autoregressive loop is omitted. Within a chunk, the video DiT's per-layer K/V over the clean first-frame tokens is cached once and reused by all 10 action steps (Fig. 1C; code prefill_video_cache)
190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D V2 32 GB (authors); the imagine-then-execute variant Fast-WAM-IDM takes 810 ms on the same GPU
Removing test-time imagination costs little accuracy while removing video co-training costs much; the deployed graph is 1 pass of the 5B DiT plus 10 passes of the 1B expert [D]

name: comma.ai world model (openpilot 0.11)
tagline: Block-causal driving DiT that trains openpilot
summary: The learned driving simulator behind openpilot 0.11, whose driving policy comma calls the first robotics agent shipped to real users that was fully trained in a learned simulation. A ViT compressor turns the two camera views into a 32x16x32 latent, and a 2B block-causal diffusion transformer predicts the next frame latent, plus future actions, from 2 s of context, 6-DoF relative-pose actions and 1 s of future frames (so it is also an inverse dynamics model). Sampling is frame by frame with 15 Euler steps and CFG 2.0; with KV caching comma reports a sampling throughput of 12.2 frames/s per GPU (GPU and batch size not stated), not a latency.
facts: ViT frame compressor (encoder 50M, decoder 100M, 2x deeper): two views (narrow, wide) of 3x128x256 → one 32x16x32 latent; DiT patch size and tokens per frame not stated (comma's later 4B world model uses 2x2 latent patches = 128 tokens per frame)

2B diffusion transformer: 48 layers, d 1600, 25 heads (n_layer=48, n_head=25, n_embd=1600), 'adapted to 3 dimensional data'; norm and MLP details not disclosed, so the MLP and the drawn block layout (AdaLN-single before attention and MLP, residual adds) are assumed from DiT/PixArt-α
Block-causal in every layer: tokens attend to their own frame and past frames; a sample = 2 s past context + 1 s future conditioning + 0-7 s simulation window at 5 fps (10 context frames [D])
6-DoF relative positions, diffusion noise level and frame indices injected via AdaLN-single (PixArt-α style)

Rectified flow with logit-normal noise sampling; frame by frame, 15 Euler steps, classifier-free guidance 2.0 (up to 30 DiT passes per frame if the conditional and unconditional branches run separately [D]); noise-level augmentation for rollout robustness
ViT decoder (100M) → narrow and wide 128x256 frames
KV cache enabled by the block-causal mask; context 2 s at 5 fps
12.2 frames/s per GPU throughput with KV caching (company claim; GPU type and batch size not stated); ≈366 DiT frame-evaluations per second per GPU at 15 steps × CFG [D]

The on-policy driving model (a small transformer) is trained to predict the world model's suggested actions on rollouts generated with the world model and the latest policy checkpoint ('near on-policy'); the world model is trained on 2.5M minutes (≈41,700 h [D]) of driving video; weights release not stated on the page

name: DreamZero
tagline: One 14B DiT denoises video and actions together
summary: A 14B world-action model: the Wan2.1-I2V-14B image-to-video DiT is fully fine-tuned into a chunk-wise autoregressive flow-matching model that denoises the next 2 latent frames of video and the matching 1.6 s action chunk together, with one shared timestep and separate output decoders. Clean context sits in a KV cache (with the chunk being denoised, at most 4 chunks plus the first frame: 33 raw frames, 6.6 s), and after each chunk executes the predicted frames are replaced by encoded real observations. Naive inference costs 5.7 s per chunk; CFG on 2 GPUs, velocity caching (16 → 4 DiT steps), compilation, kernel and scheduler tuning, NVFP4 and the 1-step DreamZero-Flash schedule bring it to 150 ms on 2 GB200.
facts: Frozen Wan2.1 VAE latents (480p model; 8x spatial, 4x temporal); 3 camera views resized to 176×320 and tiled 2×2 into one frame (code); 880 tokens per latent frame (DreamZero checkpoint config frame_seqlen); a full context of 33 raw frames encodes to 9 latent frames, the first frame plus 4 chunks of 2 [D: 33 = 1 + 4×8]

Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P DiT with all blocks fine-tuned: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13,824 (base config.json); only state and action encoders plus an action decoder are added; text encoder, image encoder and VAE stay frozen; block internals not detailed in the paper (LayerNorm and RoPE named in its quantization notes)

Chunk-causal: the noisy current chunk (K = 2 latent frames + its action chunk) attends to the clean previous chunks; frames inside a chunk share one timestep; max context 8 latent frames (4 chunks) = 6.6 s

Action latents denoised jointly with the video in the same DiT, same timestep; chunks of 48 actions at 30 Hz (AgiBot) or 24 at 15 Hz (DROID) = 1.6 s; relative joint positions, Savitzky-Golay smoothed; the action encoder embeds the noisy actions with the timestep, the state encoder (2-layer MLP) adds one state token per chunk to the DiT sequence, and the action decoder (2-layer MLP) maps the action tokens to the action velocity at every step (code)

Flow matching: 16 steps baseline → 4 effective with velocity caching (cached velocity reused when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold) → 1 step with DreamZero-Flash (video timesteps biased to high noise, t = 1 − Beta(7,1); action timesteps uniform)

Wan2.1 VAE decoder turns predicted latents into future frames (Fig. 4 inference panel); not needed for control: actions come straight from the denoised action chunk, predicted video latents are discarded, and the released server decodes them only to save videos

KV cache refreshed with VAE-encoded real observations after every chunk (clean t = 0 pass; predicted frames discarded); it holds the first frame plus up to 3 earlier chunks (≤ 7 latent frames [D]), so with the chunk being denoised the window is 9 latent frames = 33 raw frames (code: local_attn_size = 4×2 + 1); cache reset every 4 chunks (code)

5.7 s per chunk naive on one GPU; with CFG split across 2 GPUs: 9.6x on H100 (~0.59 s [D]), 16.6x with NVFP4 (~350 ms at 4 steps) and 38x with Flash (150 ms at 1 step, ~7 Hz) on GB200 (company claims, Tables 1 and 3)

Generating only actions gives a minimal speed-up at 14B (diffusion steps and DiT blocks dominate latency); the 38x comes from fewer DiT passes (16 → 4 by caching, → 1 with Flash), 2-GPU CFG, torch.compile + CUDA graphs, cuDNN attention + GPU-side scheduler, and NVFP4 (E2M1 weights and activations, FP8 QKV and softmax)

name: LingBot-World-Fast
tagline: Causal Wan DiT that keeps the whole rollout in KV
summary: A real-time open world model: the high-noise expert of the middle-trained LingBot-World MoE (Wan2.2 I2V A14B architecture, two ≈14B experts, one active per timestep) is adapted to block-causal attention and distilled with DMD plus an adversarial head to 4 steps. In the released checkpoint, camera poses enter as Plücker-style ray maps through scale-and-shift adapters in every block (≈18.5B parameters in all); the paper's W/A/S/D-key variant is the Base (Act) model. By default it keeps the full KV cache of the whole rollout, so memory is emergent from context, but the cache grows by about 3.4 GB per 12-frame chunk and throughput falls from 8.9 to 3.6 FPS over a minute (WorldKV, 4×B200). The company claims 16 fps at 480p on one GPU node; the release script uses 8 GPUs.
facts: Wan 3D causal VAE, stride 4x8x8 → 60x104 latent frame at 480x832; patch (1,2,2) → 1,560 tokens (30x52 grid) per latent frame [D]; chunk = 3 latent frames = 4,680 tokens = 12 output frames, 9 for the first chunk [D]

Wan2.2 I2V A14B config: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13824; initialized from the high-noise expert of the middle-trained LingBot-World MoE (two ≈14B experts, one active per timestep), a dense causal DiT: 18.54B in the released checkpoint (14.29B Wan backbone + 4.26B camera layers; 14B in the paper)
Block-causal: bidirectional within a chunk, causal across chunks, KV cache; local_attn_size -1 and sink_size 0 by default = full KV over the whole rollout (window and sink exist as flags)

Released Fast: camera poses → per-pixel [ray origin, ray direction] → Plücker encoder (Linear 1536→5120 + residual MLP) → per-block MLP → scale and shift of the residual stream (no norm). The paper's rotation Plücker + multi-hot W/A/S/D keys is the Base (Act) variant; in Stage II only the action adapters were trained

DMD with self-rollout plus an adversarial head on the fake-score network (APT-style, no R1/R2); 4 steps at indices [0, 179, 358, 679] of the 1,000-step schedule, shift 10 in the release CLI (generate() default 5); the bidirectional base samples 70 steps
Wan VAE decoder at 480x832, 12 frames per chunk (9 for the first); the release decodes all chunks in one call after the rollout loop (README lists 480P & 720P)
No memory module: 'an emergent ability derived from the context window'; full KV ≈3.4 GB per 3-latent-frame chunk and >200 GB per minute (WorldKV; ≈3.8 GB per chunk by my count [D])

16 fps at 480p with <1 s latency on one GPU node (company claim; release script uses 8 GPUs with Ulysses sequence parallelism, GPU type not stated); WorldKV on 4×B200: 8.87 → 3.61 FPS over a one-minute rollout with full KV, WorldKV Table 1 at the last chunk of a rollout: 3.83 FPS vs 8.10 with a sliding window (4×H200: 2.36 vs 5.05)

name: LingBot-VA
tagline: Interleaves video and actions in one causal sequence
summary: A causal world-action model that interleaves video latents and actions in one autoregressive sequence with a KV cache. Two parallel transformer streams of the same depth, a 5B video stream initialised from Wan2.2-5B (d 3072) and a 0.35B action stream (d 768), are joined by shared attention. Each step denoises the next chunk (K = 4) with 3 Euler steps only to s = 0.6 (partial denoising, enabled by noisy-history augmentation), then decodes the chunk's actions (τK = 16 by the paper's formula) as inverse dynamics in 10 steps; real observations re-enter the cache in closed loop.
facts: Wan2.2 causal VAE (4x16x16) plus 2x patchify; all camera views concatenated along the width → 192 spatial tokens per latent frame; video at 12.5 Hz with 4 actions per frame (50 Hz)

MoT: video stream from Wan2.2-5B, 30 layers, d 3072 (24 heads, FFN 14,336 per the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config); action stream of the same depth at d 768 (~350M), initialised by interpolating the video weights scaled by sqrt(d_v/d_a); RoPE in both; T5 text through cross-attention (which stream reads it is not stated); norms and timestep modulation not given in the paper

Causal over the interleaved video-action sequence (teacher forcing), bidirectional inside a chunk; action tokens are projected to d 3072 for the joint attention and back; training packs episodes into sequences of up to 10K tokens

Action tokens in the sequence (single-layer MLP encoder and decoder, hidden 256; quantile-normalised), decoded by inverse dynamics conditioned on the predicted visual transition; chunk K = 4 video frames = τK = 16 actions by the paper's formula [D]; released configs give 16-80 actions per chunk

Flow matching with an Euler solver: video 3 steps to s = 0.6 (partial denoising) at CFG 5.0, actions 10 steps to s = 1.0 at CFG 1.0; a forward-dynamics step re-grounds the cache on the latest real frame
Wan2.2 VAE decoder exists for visualisation, but actions are read from latents and the partially denoised video is never decoded for control

Causal KV cache over the interleaved history (released server: FIFO of the last 36 chunks for RoboTwin, 15 otherwise); the async-pipeline prose limits the active context to the last step, but Alg. 2 and Sec. 4.5.2 keep all cached history
Not disclosed: no latency, control rate or GPU is given; the authors name video-token denoising as the primary inference bottleneck

Per chunk: 3 video steps x 2 CFG passes = 6 passes of the 5B stream over the new video tokens (768 if K = 4 latent frames of 192), plus 10 passes of the 0.35B stream, plus a cache-write pass over the encoded real frames and executed actions [D]

name: Cosmos Policy
tagline: Video DiT predicts actions as extra latent frames
summary: Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World, a latent video diffusion transformer over Wan2.1 VAE latents, fully fine-tuned into a robot policy with no architectural change. Proprioception, the action chunk and the value are injected as extra latent frames: blank images are VAE-encoded and their latents overwritten with tiled copies of the vectors, so the denoising process that predicts future images also predicts actions. As a direct policy it denoises everything in parallel in 5 steps on LIBERO and RoboCasa (0.61 s per chunk on one H100; 10 steps and 0.95 s on ALOHA) and discards the future state and value; planning mode decodes them autoregressively for best-of-N search.
facts: Wan2.1 VAE latent frames (8x spatial, 4x temporal, 16 channels); one latent frame per modality and camera view, e.g. 9 for LIBERO (blank, proprio, 2 views, action chunk, future proprio, 2 future views, value) or 11 with 3 cameras; each image is repeated 4x so one latent frame is one timestep; LIBERO data at 224 px per the repo config, i.e. ~196 tokens per latent frame with the 2x2 patch [D]

Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World DiT, all weights fine-tuned: 28 blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, patch 2x2x1, 3D RoPE, AdaLN-LoRA timestep conditioning (repo net config COSMOS_V1_2B); T5 text via cross-attention; no new modules; Predict1 block design with QK RMSNorm
Bidirectional 3D self-attention over all latent frames; clean conditioning frames (current state) and noisy target frames share the sequence

The action chunk (K x d_act, scaled to [-1, 1], flattened and duplicated to fill H' x W' x C') overwrites a placeholder latent frame and is read back by averaging the copies; K = 16 (LIBERO, all executed), 32 (RoboCasa, 16 executed), 50 at 25 Hz (ALOHA)

EDM denoising with sigma_max 80 and sigma_min 4: 5 steps (LIBERO, RoboCasa) or 10 (ALOHA) with action, future state and value in parallel, the latter two discarded; planning: autoregressive 10 + 5 + 5 steps, ensembles of 3 states and 5 values, best-of-N = 8
Wan2.1 VAE decoder only to visualise predicted future images; actions and values are read from the latents without any decoding
None: the input is the current observation only, no history; 6.0-8.9 GB VRAM at inference without planning (README)
Per action chunk on one H100 (authors): 0.61 s at 5 steps, 0.95 s at 10, 0.16 s at 1 step (RoboCasa still 66.4% success at 1 step); best-of-8 planning 4.9 s on 8 parallel H100s
Every step also denoises the future-state and value frames the policy throws away

name: WorldPlay (HY-World 1.5)
tagline: Causal DiT with memory retrieved by camera view
summary: Tencent's real-time interactive world model: the HunyuanVideo-1.5 MM-DiT made chunk-wise block-causal (4 latent frames = 16 video frames per chunk) and distilled with Context Forcing to 4 steps. Each chunk attends to a memory rebuilt from the 3 most recent chunks, 1 chunk retrieved by field-of-view overlap and camera distance, and the first chunk kept as an attention sink, with RoPE indices re-assigned so old frames look recent. Keys enter through the timestep embedding, camera pose through a relative encoding inside attention. The company's 24 FPS at 720p needs 8 H800 GPUs with token parallelism, quantization and streaming VAE decode.
facts: HunyuanVideo-1.5 causal 3D VAE: 16x spatial, 4x temporal, 32 channels; patch 1x1x1 → 3,600 tokens per latent frame at 720p, 14,400 per 4-latent chunk of 16 frames [D]

HunyuanVideo-1.5 480P-I2V transformer: 54 double-stream MM-DiT blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4, GELU-tanh (HF config); no cross-attention in the released code: text tokens (2-layer token refiner) run in a parallel stream whose K/V join the video attention; timestep adaLN; 8B per the README (a 5B Wan-based variant is lighter but weaker)

Block-causal over chunks with a KV cache; context = 3 temporal + 1 spatial chunk + the first chunk as attention sink = 20 latents = 72,000 tokens at 720p (86,400 with the current chunk) [D]; temporal reframing re-assigns RoPE indices so context frames sit at a small relative distance

Dual representation: discrete keys → PE + zero-initialized MLP added to the timestep embedding (adaLN); camera pose → PRoPE relative encoding in a second attention term, output = Attn1 + zero_init(Attn2)
Flow matching; Context Forcing distillation (memory-augmented bidirectional teacher, DMD loss) from 100 NFE to 4 denoising steps per 16-frame chunk
HunyuanVideo-1.5 VAE decoder → 16 frames per chunk; progressive decode in small batches streamed over Triton, parallelized over 8 GPUs; the open checkpoints are 480P

Reconstituted context memory rebuilt per chunk by FOV-overlap and camera-distance retrieval from past chunks; no explicit 3D state; its KV cache is recomputed in one extra pass per chunk; KV ≈63.7 GB in BF16 for the 72,000-token context (RoPE and PRoPE K/V both cached), ≈8.0 GB per GPU when split 8 ways [D]

24 FPS at 720p on 8×H800 (company claim); Table 4: 2.80 → 3.80 (DiT parallelism + quantization) → 16.0 (+VAE) → 24.0 FPS (+streaming decode); 4.95 FPS for the 8B model on 4×H200 (measured by WorldKV); 28 GB per GPU at sp=8 (README)
Distillation cuts passes 25x, but the remaining 8.57x to real time is systems work; ≈90% of per-chunk DiT FLOPs is attention: two attention terms (RoPE and PRoPE) per block over ≈86,400 tokens [D]

name: Cosmos-Predict2.5
tagline: Bidirectional DiT that generates whole video clips
summary: NVIDIA's physical-AI world foundation model: a flow-matching DiT that generates a whole 93-frame clip (24 latent frames, 5.8 s at 16 fps) with full self-attention, unifying Text2World, Image2World and Video2World by replacing conditioning frames in the sequence and flagging them with a mask token. The Cosmos-Reason1 VLM replaces T5 as the text encoder. It is a clip generator, not an interactive model: no action input in the base model (an action-conditioned robot variant exists), no KV cache, and 4-step distillation (rCM in the paper; the released 2B Text2World checkpoint is configured as DMD2). The 2B model card reports 228.8 s per 720p Video2World clip on H100 SXM.

Full (bidirectional) self-attention over all tokens of the clip; training at 720p/93 frames uses context parallelism 2 (2B) or 8 (14B) (Table 9)

None in the base model: conditioning is text (Cosmos-Reason1 multi-block activations projected to 1024-d, via cross-attention) and 1 or 5 conditioning frames concatenated with a mask-token flag; the 2B robot/action-cond variant adds an action-embedder MLP to the timestep embeddings (Sec. 6.6), and the 7-camera driving variant concatenates views along the latent time axis (Sec. 6.3.1)

Flow matching; the paper distills with rCM (continuous-time consistency + distribution matching) to 4 steps, 2B overall score 0.768 → 0.764 (Table 7); the released 4-step 2B checkpoint (Text2World only) is configured as DMD2 in TrigFlow form; the released base sampler defaults to 35 FlowUniPC steps with CFG 7 (two passes per step)

name: Dreamer 4
tagline: Few-step space-time transformer with agent heads
summary: A scalable world model that trains a Minecraft agent entirely offline inside its own imagination. A 400M block-causal transformer tokenizer (masked autoencoding, continuous tanh bottleneck) turns each 360x640 frame into 512 latent tokens of 16 channels, which the dynamics model reshapes into 256 spatial tokens of 32 channels. A 1.6B block-causal dynamics transformer, factorized over space and time with temporal attention in every 4th layer and GQA, denoises the next frame's tokens with a shortcut-forcing objective in K = 4 passes. The context is 192 frames (9.6 s), the model runs at 21 FPS on one H100, and policy, reward and value heads read agent tokens inside the same transformer.
facts: 256 spatial tokens x 32 channels per frame (a 512x16 bottleneck reshaped) from a 400M block-causal MAE tokenizer with a continuous tanh bottleneck; 384x640 padded input = 960 patches of 16x16

1.6B dynamics transformer: pre-RMSNorm, RoPE (layers and axes not given), SwiGLU, QKNorm, attention logit soft-capping; layer, head and width counts not disclosed in the paper; repeat unit of 3 space layers + 1 causal time layer (Fig. 2b); the drawn residual adds and one SwiGLU MLP per layer are assumed (standard pre-norm layout)
Block-causal: all tokens of a frame attend to each other and to the past; space-only and time-only layers, temporal attention every 4th layer, GQA; context 192 frames = 49,152 spatial tokens [D]

Interleaved tokens: each action component (mouse, keyboard) is encoded into S_a tokens and summed with a learned embedding; each frame block also carries S_r registers and one shortcut signal-level/step-size token

Shortcut forcing (diffusion forcing + shortcut models, x-prediction, ramp loss weight): K = 4 passes per frame instead of 64, no separate distillation; rollouts stay in latent space, and context latents, generated ones included, are re-noised to tau_ctx = 0.1
The tokenizer's block-causal transformer decoder, frame by frame, to 360x640
KV cache over 192 frames (9.6 s); size not computable from the disclosed numbers; the authors name MLP FLOPs and KV-cache bandwidth as the inference limits
21 FPS at 640x360 on one H100 (authors, Table 1); the design cascade runs 0.8 → 9.1 (4-step shortcut) → 18.9 (temporal attention every 4 layers) → 23.2 (GQA) → … → 21.4 FPS at 256 tokens (Table 2)

Agent tokens attend to everything but nothing attends back to them, so policy, reward and value heads share the world model's trunk and read the agent-token outputs; the transformer stays frozen during imagination training

name: CWM (Code World Model)
summary: A 32B dense decoder-only LLM mid-trained on observation-action trajectories: Python execution traces (stack-frame locals after each executed line) and agentic Docker sessions. The same transformer is policy and world model; a world-model step is ordinary text generation of the next observation. For compute it is plain long-context LLM decoding, kept affordable by GQA and a 3:1 local/global pattern (47 layers with an 8k window, 17 with 131k) that allows a KV cache of about 10 GiB per 131k-token sequence when the local layers keep only their window [D].
tagline: Code LLM trained to predict execution traces
facts: Text and code tokens, Llama 3 BPE tokenizer, vocabulary 128,256; an observation is the stack-frame locals as JSON, an action is the Python line executed (custom separator tokens)
Dense decoder-only: 64 layers, d 6144, FFN 21,504 (SwiGLU), 48 query heads of 128, 8 KV heads (GQA), RMSNorm pre-norm; 32B parameters

Document-causal; local sliding window 8,192 tokens and global window 131,072 tokens interleaved 3:1, with the last layer also global: 47 local + 17 global layers (global at 0, 4, …, 60 and 63; Fig. 6a, config); scaled RoPE in every layer, θ 1M, scale factor 16
Actions are text in the stream (a Python statement or an agent tool call); the next observation is generated as text after it
Next-token softmax over 128k vocabulary; one pass per token, so one trace step costs as many passes as its frame has tokens (locals JSON, separators and the source line)
None; the output is text (trace frames, code, tool calls)

KV cache per token per layer 4 KiB in bf16 (K and V, 8 KV heads × 128); at 131k context 8.5 GiB for the 17 global layers + 1.47 GiB for the 47 local layers (8k window) ≈ 10 GiB, vs 32 GiB if every layer kept the full context [D]; the released FastGen engine (paged attention, host-side KV cache) keeps full-length KV in all 64 layers, 256 KiB per token [D]
No decode-throughput figure; inference fits one 80 GB H100 with quantization (authors; bf16 weights alone are 65 GB [D]); trained on 2,048 H100s for pre- and mid-training (Table 3)

13T pre- and mid-training tokens, the last 5T in the code-world-model mid-training stage at 131k context (trace and agent data are 30% of that mix); the world model is the LLM itself, so running it is long-context LLM decoding

name: Genie Envisioner (GE-Act)
tagline: Thin action DiT reads a video DiT's cached latents
summary: A two-stream world-action model on top of GE-Base, an instruction-conditioned multi-view video DiT built from LTX-Video 2B and pretrained on ~3,000 h of AgiBot-World-Beta. GE-Act adds a parallel 160M action branch with the same depth but a smaller hidden size; it reads the visual latents of every GE-Base block through cross-attention and denoises a 54-step action trajectory by flow matching. At deployment the video DiT runs a single denoising step whose latents are cached, the action branch runs 5 steps, and a 54-step trajectory comes out in 200 ms on a robot-mounted RTX 4090.
facts: Frozen LTX video-VAE latents of three views (head, left wrist, right wrist); 4 conditioning frames per view (sparse memory, the last being the current frame in the code), each one latent frame, plus 2 predicted latent frames from 9-frame clips at 5 Hz; 48 tokens per latent frame per view at 192x256 (32x VAE, patch 1) [D], so 288 per view and 864 for 3 views [D]

GE-Base: LTX-Video 2B DiT (28 layers, 32 heads of 64 = d 2048 [D]); RoPE on Q/K (paper: 2D; code: 3D over latent frame, H, W); in code the view embedding is added to the AdaLN-single timestep modulation (shift, scale, gate), RMSNorm without affine before self-attention and FFN, un-normalised text cross-attention, GELU-tanh FFN; GE-Act: same block design, 28 blocks, width 512 (16 heads x 32) in the policy config, 160M parameters

Video: unmasked self-attention over all (T, H, W) tokens of each view; in every third block (10 of 28 [D]) over all 3 views jointly (code; the paper says selected blocks); T5-XXL instruction via cross-attention; GE-Act action tokens cross-attend to every block's video hidden states, all views concatenated

54-step trajectories at 30 Hz of 14-D dual-arm actions (released AgiBot config: per-step end-effector xyz/rpy deltas + gripper; the paper intro calls them torque trajectories), denoised by flow matching from noise-initialised action tokens; a new action DiT is trained from scratch for each new embodiment
Slow-fast asynchronous inference: 1 flow-matching step of the video DiT with its latents cached, then 5 action denoising steps on that cache; video DiT at 5 Hz vs action model at 30 Hz (1:6)
Frozen video VAE decoder, used when GE-Base / GE-Sim generate video; GE-Act deployment skips video decoding (return_video=False), though the paper also shows GE-Act generating videos
Sparse memory: 4 conditioning frames per view (code: 3 sampled earlier frames plus the current one), each one latent frame; the paper's GE-Base text counts the initial frame separately

54-step trajectory in 200 ms on an onboard RTX 4090 mounted on the robot (authors), i.e. 5 chunks/s [D]; training: GE-Base-MR 32 A100 x ~7 days, GE-Base-LF 32 A100 x ~3 days, GE-Act pretraining 16 A100 x ~3 days
Partial video denoising in deployment: one 2B video pass plus 5 passes of a thin action DiT per trajectory [D]

name: EMERALD
summary: A Dreamer-style agent with a spatial latent state. A CNN VAE encodes each 64x64 frame as a 4x4 grid of 32-way categoricals in 32 groups, a temporal transformer with one token per step carries the history, and a small spatial MaskGIT transformer predicts the next 4x4 grid in S = 3 parallel refinement passes instead of 512 serial token decodes (4x4 positions x 32 groups). name: WorldVLA
tagline: One LLM writes next-frame and action tokens
summary: A single autoregressive transformer, initialised from Chameleon, that treats images, text and actions as one token vocabulary: it predicts the next frame's VQ-GAN codes as a world model and the next action's 7 tokens as a VLA, and the authors report that training both together helps both. name: AAPT
tagline: Causal DiT, one adversarial pass per latent frame
summary: Autoregressive Adversarial Post-Training, the one-pass-per-frame design: a pre-trained 8B video diffusion transformer is made block-causal and post-trained adversarially so that each latent frame (4 video frames) is generated with a single network evaluation from noise, the previous generated frame recycled through channel concatenation, and a KV cache over a sliding window of 30 latent frames. Per-frame conditions (human pose, or camera rays relative to the previous frame) enter as extra input channels. The authors report 24 fps at 736x416 on one H100 with 0.16 s latency, or 1280x720 on 8 H100s, for streams up to a minute.

summary: An action-conditioned autoregressive video diffusion model whose backbone swaps full attention for a hybrid: a block-wise Mamba scan carries long-term memory across frames in a fixed-size state, and frame-local attention keeps nearby frames sharp. tagline: Two timesteps turn one DiT into policy or dynamics

name: TWISTER
summary: DreamerV3 with its GRU replaced by a small Transformer State-Space Model and an extra action-conditioned contrastive objective. A CNN VAE encodes 64x64 frames as 32x32 categoricals, an action mixer fuses state and action into one token, and a 4-block causal transformer with Transformer-XL relative positions predicts the next state, reward and continuation. The cache is capped at 8 steps, so per-step memory is bounded. Swapping in the transformer alone scores like DreamerV3; the gain comes from AC-CPC, which predicts features 10 steps ahead given the future actions and helps the transformer far more than DreamerV3's RSSM (mean HNS 162 vs 121).

tagline: Factorized-attention DiT over five cameras
summary: Wayve's multi-camera driving world model: a video tokenizer with 32x spatial and 8x temporal compression turns up to 5 camera streams into 64-channel latents, and an 8.4B space-time factorized transformer denoises them with flow matching. The ego action and flow-matching time enter through adaptive LayerNorm; 3D agent boxes, scene and road-layout metadata and CLIP or scenario embeddings through cross-attention; camera geometry and timestamps as added encodings. It runs 50 denoising steps; Wayve describes no KV cache, reports no inference speed and lists distillation and faster, near-real-time synthesis as future work.
facts: Video tokenizer (space-time factorized transformer, 85M encoder / 200M decoder): 8x temporal, 32x spatial, 64 channels; 24 frames at 448x960 → 3x14x30 latents (≈400x compression); 420 latents per camera per latent step, 2,100 across 5 cameras [D]

22 space-time factorized transformer blocks, d 4096, 32 heads, 8.4B parameters; each block adds the position, timestamp and camera encodings, then runs spatial attention (over space and cameras), temporal attention, cross-attention and an MLP with adaptive LayerNorm; QK-norm before each attention. Assumed in the diagram (not described): adaptive LayerNorm before each attention layer and the residual connections, as in DiT

Factorized: spatial attention over 2,100 tokens (5 cameras × 420) [D], temporal attention over 6 latent steps; training window 48 frames × 5 cameras = 12,600 tokens; no full 3D attention; sinusoidal space and timestamp encodings plus learned camera geometry, re-added at the start of every block

Ego-vehicle action (speed, curvature) and flow-matching time via adaptive LayerNorm in every block (found more accurate than cross-attention); 3D agent boxes, metadata (incl. road layout) and CLIP or scenario embeddings via cross-attention; camera geometry and timestamps are added to the latents with the positional encodings

Flow matching, 50 denoising steps, linear-quadratic schedule, no distillation; CFG off by default (scale 2-20 for hard cases); rollout in latent space: k=3 context latents, predict the next set of latents (3 per stride in Fig. 2), append, slide the window
200M decoder with 24 space-time factorized blocks (16 + 8, d 512, 16 heads): jointly decodes 3 latent steps into 24 frames at 448x960 per camera; sliding window at inference
Sliding window of latents; no KV cache described

Not disclosed; 'real-time or near-real-time video synthesis remains computationally intensive', distillation listed as future work (authors); ≈1.1e16 dense FLOPs per 50-step, 48-frame, 5-camera window [D]

Wayve chose 32x spatial / 64-channel latents because shorter latent sequences give faster inference and better memory efficiency, and the model captures dynamics better; ≈1.5e12 training tokens on 256 H100s [D]

name: WHAM (Muse)
tagline: Game frames and controller tokens, one at a time
summary: World and Human Action Model: a nanoGPT-style causal transformer trained from scratch on seven years of Bleeding Edge gameplay to predict interleaved image and controller-action tokens. The 1.6B model sees 540 ViT-VQGAN tokens per 300x180 frame (vocabulary 16,384) plus 16 action tokens, with a 1 s context of ten frames = 5,560 tokens. Generation is token by token, more than 540 serial passes per frame, which is why Microsoft followed it with a MaskGIT variant (WHAMM, 10+ fps against about 1 fps).
facts: 540 discrete tokens per 300x180 frame from a ~300M ViT-VQGAN, vocabulary 16,384 (1.6B model); the 15M-894M models use 256 tokens per 128x128 frame from a ~60M conv VQGAN, vocabulary 4,096
Modified nanoGPT implementation of GPT-2, 1.6B parameters (also 15M-894M); 24 layers, 18 heads, width 2304, FFN 9216 (released code)
Dense causal over 5,560 tokens = 1 s = 10 frames at 10 Hz (2,720 tokens for the 894M model)

Xbox controller as 16 tokens per step [D: (5,560 - 10 x 540) / 10]: 12 buttons plus the x and y of both sticks discretized into 11 buckets; no delimiter token, the learned positions tell the modalities apart; actions are predicted as well as consumed
Next-token softmax: at least 540 serial passes per frame plus the 16 action tokens [D]
Released code: KV cache within a step (prefill the window, then one cached pass per token), rebuilt for each modality (image, then action); 1 s window of 10 steps slides, positions restart at 0

About 1 fps for WHAM-1.6B against 10+ fps for the MaskGIT-based WHAMM (Microsoft Research WHAMM article, 4 Apr 2025; the Nature paper gives no inference figure). Training: 200k updates x 2.5M tokens = 5e11 tokens [D]; 98 H100s, 5 days (HF model card)

556 sequential tokens per frame at 1.6B with a 5,560-token context: per-frame decode like GAIA-1 (576 image tokens, 6.5B) at a quarter of its size and about a third of its 15,860-token context [D]; the fix was MaskGIT decoding (WHAMM)

name: UVA (Unified Video Action)
tagline: Video and action heads on one masked transformer
summary: A masked-autoencoder-style transformer, initialised from MAR-B, that fuses a history of kl-f16 VAE latents and action chunks into a joint video-action latent, which two lightweight diffusion heads decode into video patches and actions. Denoising runs only in the small heads, never in the backbone, and at deployment the video head is skipped entirely, so a 16-action trajectory costs 95 ms on an RTX 3080: 40 ms of VAE encoding, 40 ms of transformer (30 with flash attention) and 15 ms for 16 steps of the action head.
facts: Pretrained kl-f16 VAE latent map (w x h x c) per frame, flattened and projected by an FC layer into N tokens of width d; official config: 256×256 frames, 16×16×16 latents, so N = 256 tokens per frame and h = 4 frames (the paper gives neither); future frames enter as randomly masked tokens concatenated channel-wise with the history tokens

MAE-style transformer initialised from MAR-B and itself mar_base (official code: 12 encoder + 12 decoder timm ViT blocks, pre-LN, d 768, 12 heads, MLP ratio 4); 0.5B parameters in total (paper, no breakdown); language (Libero10, UMI multi-task) is a CLIP ViT-B/32 text token projected 512 → 768, repeated M times (64 in code) and concatenated into the token sequence; the paper calls this cross-attention, but the code has no cross-attention layer

Bidirectional (no attention mask in code) over the N x h video-action tokens + M language tokens; the same positions are masked in every frame to avoid leakage; the paper says attention takes half of the inference time; Table VI: transformer 40 of 95 ms, 30 with flash attention
Each frame pairs with a chunk of L actions sampled faster than frames; history chunks are repeated M times, FC-projected to N action tokens and concatenated channel-wise with the visual tokens

Video: MAR-style masked generation from an empty sequence in 1 to 8 autoregressive stages; actions: a conv + MLP pool the N latents into one action latent that conditions the action diffusion head, 16 denoising steps on the robot (100 in simulation)
Video diffusion head + VAE decoder exist but are skipped at deployment (100 ms at 16 steps, 625 ms at 100)
History window of h frames and action chunks; no KV cache

Per 16-action trajectory on an RTX 3080 (authors, Table VI): VAE encoder 40 ms, transformer 40 ms (30 with flash attention), action head 15 ms at 16 steps (93 at 100); total 95 ms (85 with flash attention), 173 ms at 100 steps; policy + planner 195 ms; simulation timings on L40

Trained with video, deployed without it: the skipped video head (100 ms) would cost more than the whole 95 ms policy, and the VAE encoder plus backbone, not the action head, dominate (80 of 95 ms [D])

name: Cosmos-Predict1 (autoregressive)
tagline: Llama-style GPT over discrete video tokens
summary: NVIDIA's autoregressive world foundation models: Llama3-style GPTs trained from scratch to predict the next video token, with no language pretraining. A discrete video tokenizer (8x16x16, FSQ, vocabulary 64,000) gives 2,560 tokens per latent frame at 640x1024, and the 4B and 12B models attend causally over 12,800 tokens (33 video frames) with 3D RoPE. The Video2World 5B/13B variants add T5 cross-attention, and Medusa heads cut the number of forward passes by up to 4.6x (4B). Generating 32 frames takes 31 s on one H100 for the 4B.
facts: Cosmos-Tokenize1-DV8x16x16 discrete tokens, FSQ levels (8,8,8,5,5,5) = vocabulary 64,000; at 640x1024 one latent frame (8 video frames; the first holds only frame 1) is 40x64 = 2,560 tokens [D]

Llama3-style decoder with SwiGLU and QK-norm: 4B = 16 layers, d 4096, FFN 14,336, 32 heads, 8 KV heads; 12B = 40 layers, d 5120; the 5B/13B Video2World models add cross-attention layers; RMSNorm (eps 1e-5) before each sub-layer plus a final RMSNorm (official code; the paper names no norm)

Dense causal over 12,800 tokens = 5 latent frames = 33 video frames, the maximum the AR variants support [D]; 3D RoPE (theta 500,000) plus a sinusoidal 3D absolute positional embedding in every block (Table 14 lists it for all four sizes; the released code adds it only for Video2World); the text says no MQA/GQA, but Table 14 and the code use 8 KV heads

The base models take only video; the Bridge robot post-train (5B ActionCond) projects the 7-D gripper action with an MLP and injects it by cross-attention; text enters by T5-XXL cross-attention in Video2World

Next-token softmax, 2,560 passes per latent frame [D]; Medusa speculative decoding (single-layer FFN heads on the last hidden state that share the output layer, no tree attention; tested on 4B/5B; the released code has no Medusa model): the chosen 9 heads give 2.0x token throughput and 4.2x fewer passes for 4B, 3.2x and 5.7x for 5B [D]; 12 heads give the fewest passes (4.6x, 6.1x) (Table 15, 8 H100)
Tokenizer decoder, or an optional 7B diffusion decoder that adds 30-32 s on one H100, doubling the 4B time (31.04 → 61.49 s) [D]

KV caching is used (Sec. 5.2.4, gpt-fast style); the code keeps a static BF16 self-attention cache over all 12,800 positions, 8 KV heads × 128 dims per layer: ≈0.84 GB per sequence for 4B, ≈2.1 GB for 12B [D]; cross-attention K/V are not cached
4B on one H100 at 640x1024, 32 frames from 1: 31.04 s (23.52 s with Medusa), 29 GB; 12B 84.78 s; 4B at 320x512 with Medusa on 8 H100: 806.61 tokens/s = 10.08 frames/s (NVIDIA, Tables 16-17)

~330 tokens/s for 4B on one H100, averaged over the whole run (10,240 generated tokens in 31.04 s) [D]; 4 → 8 GPUs gains only 3% (18.20 → 17.62 s) [D]; the 10 FPS result used 4x fewer tokens per frame (320x512) [D], Medusa and 8 H100s

name: Navigation World Model (CDiT)
tagline: Navigation DiT that cross-attends to past frames
summary: A navigation world model for robots that predicts the next egocentric frame latent from past frames and a 3-DoF navigation action. Its Conditional Diffusion Transformer runs self-attention only over the tokens of the frame being denoised and reads the 4 context frames through cross-attention, so cost is linear in the context length (about 4x fewer FLOPs than a DiT over all frames). Planning is model-predictive control with the cross-entropy method, or ranking 32 trajectories from an external policy. The default 250 denoising steps make a 4 s trajectory cost 30.3 s on an RTX 6000 Ada; distillation to 6 steps and time skipping bring it to 0.4 s (authors).
facts: Stable Diffusion VAE (sd-vae-ft-ema) latents of 224×224 frames (4:3 centre crop, then resize): 4×28×28 latent, 2×2 patches → 196 tokens per frame (code) [D]; rollouts at 4 FPS

CDiT-XL, 1B parameters (sizes S to XL); XL/2 = 28 blocks, width 1152, 16 heads, patch 2, MLP ratio 4, the DiT-XL/2 shape (code); block = self-attention over the target frame, cross-attention to context frames with a skip connection, MLP; AdaLN scale, shift and gates

Self-attention within the target frame only (n tokens); cross-attention from target queries to the tokens of m = 4 context frames as keys and values; cost O(m n² d) vs O(m² n² d) for a full DiT; CDiT-L is 4x faster than DiT-XL at equal parameters with better prediction

Navigation action a = (u ∈ R² translation, yaw φ): each scalar → sine-cosine features → 2-layer MLP to d/3 dims, concatenated into ψ_a; time shift k (up to ±16 s) and diffusion timestep t each embedded to R^d the same way; ξ = ψ_a + ψ_k + ψ_t drives AdaLN; actions omitted for unlabeled Ego4D training

DDPM with the DiT noise schedule and learned covariance (VLB loss); 250 denoising steps by default, distilled to 6 (FastVideo DiT distillation); 'Time Skip' composes adjacent action pairs to simulate 8 instead of 16 states for 4 s
SD VAE decoder → pixels, used for LPIPS goal scoring during planning and for visualization
4 context frames re-encoded as cross-attention keys and values at every step; no KV cache discussed; loses context on out-of-distribution data (mode collapse noted by the authors)

One 4 s trajectory (16 states) on one RTX 6000 Ada: 30.3 s default → 14.7 s with Time Skip (8 states) → 0.4 s with 6-step distillation → 0.1 s with 4-bit quantization (estimated, not measured) (authors, Table 8); ≈7.4-8.3 ms per pass in the three measured configurations, ≈2.1 ms implied by the 4-bit estimate [D]; trained on 64 H100s (8 machines × 8 GPUs)

All of the ≈76x speedup comes from fewer passes (4,000 → 48: 250 → 6 steps, 16 → 8 states), none from cheaper passes; ranking 32 trajectories costs 32 × 8 × 6 = 1,536 passes per decision, run as 48 sequential batch-32 passes [D]

name: DINO-WM
tagline: Predicts DINOv2 patch features, plans by CEM
summary: A task-agnostic latent world model that predicts future DINOv2 patch features instead of pixels. A frozen DINOv2 turns each 196x196 frame into 196 patch features of width 384, and a small ViT predictor (6 layers, ~19M parameters) regresses the next frame's features from a history of up to 3 frames, with the action and proprioception embeddings concatenated onto every patch vector rather than added as tokens. Goals are images; planning is cross-entropy-method search in feature space, and the pixel decoder exists only for visualization.
facts: 196 patch features (14x14 x 384) per frame resized to 196x196, from a frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (dinov2_vits14 in the official config; the paper does not name the variant)

ViT with the patch-embedding layer removed, used as a decoder-only predictor: depth 6, 16 heads, MLP 2048, ~19M parameters (paper; the predictors in the released checkpoints have 20.1M at H = 3 and 19.96M at H = 1 [D]); token width 404 = 384 features + 10-d action + 10-d proprio (official code); the code also uses pre-LayerNorm blocks, GELU in the MLP, a learned absolute position embedding per (frame, patch) slot added once at the input, and a final LayerNorm, none of which the paper describes

Frame-level causal mask: every patch of frame t attends to all patches of frames t-H..t-1 (no token-level autoregression); H = 3 (PointMaze, Reacher, Push-T, PushObj) or 1 (Wall, Rope, Granular); at most 3 x 196 = 588 tokens [D]

A linear layer (a 1x1 Conv1d in the official code and weights; the paper calls it an MLP) maps the frameskip-stacked action to a 10-d embedding that is concatenated to every patch vector (channels, not tokens); proprioception enters the same way through its own 10-d linear layer; frameskip 5 (1 for Rope and Granular)
One pass regresses the next frame's 196 features (MSE in latent space); no sampling, no pixels
Optional transposed-convolution decoder trained separately, for visualization only; training the predictor through its loss lowers Push-T success (0.92 → 0.80)
Fixed window of H frames; no KV cache or long-term memory

One world-model forward step at batch 32: 0.014 s; a full CEM plan (100 samples x 10 iterations): 15.89 s in the ICML 2025 camera-ready (App. A.6, Table 11; arXiv v2 Table 10 gave 53.0 s), both on one A6000 (authors); LeWM later measured 47 s per DINO-WM plan in its own CEM setup (hardware not stated)

196 tokens per frame make each CEM sample a 5-step predictor rollout (released horizon 5) whose window grows from 196 to 588 tokens at H = 3, with all samples of an iteration run as one batch [D]; LeWM's one-token-per-frame design runs the same kind of plan in ~1 s (0.98 s vs 47 s in LeWM's measurement)

name: SOLD
tagline: Dreamer-style RL that imagines in object slots
summary: Dreamer-style model-based RL on object slots instead of one holistic latent. A SAVi encoder (pretrained, then fine-tuned) turns each frame into 2-10 slots of 128-d; an OCVP-Seq dynamics transformer predicts the next slot set from the slot history and the actions; three separate Slot Aggregation Transformers (reward, value, actor), each with per-step output tokens and its own MLP head, read the slot history, and the actor-critic trains on 15-step imagined slot rollouts. Each imagined step runs the dynamics model and the actor's SAT in sequence, with cost set by the slot count rather than the image resolution.
facts: N = 2-10 object slots of 128-d per frame from SAVi (learned slot init, 3 Slot Attention iterations on the first frame, 1 afterwards); slots projected to 256-d tokens; frame size not stated in the text

Dynamics: OCVP-Seq transformer encoder, 4 layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512; in code each layer is a relational and a temporal pre-LayerNorm sub-layer, each with its own ReLU FFN. One Slot Aggregation Transformer (SAT) each for reward, value and actor: 4 causal layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512, RMSNorm (SiLU FFN in code); 12M parameters in total

Dynamics (OCVP-Seq order, as in code): relational attention (the N slots plus the action token of one step) then temporal attention (each token over its own history). SAT: causal over time with ALiBi recency bias; 1 [out] + 4 [reg] tokens per step (paper; the released config uses 0 [reg]); no token can attend to earlier steps' [out]/[reg] tokens
4-D end-effector + gripper commands a_0:t are inputs to the dynamics transformer alongside the slot history (the embedding mechanism is not spelled out in the paper)

One pass predicts all N next slots (regression): joint-embedding loss to SAVi slots of the real next frame plus image reconstruction through the SAVi decoder; no teacher forcing; S seed frames then T = 15 imagined steps
SAVi CNN spatial-broadcast decoder: per-slot RGB + alpha masks composited by weighted sum; used in the dynamics loss and for visualisation, not by the actor
The dynamics model and SAT re-read the slot history each step (S + imagined steps); no KV cache mentioned
No inference or wall-clock figure; everything trains on one A100 40 GB (authors)

Reward, value and actor are MLP heads on SAT [out] tokens, with symlog two-hot reward/value bins (255 over [−20, 20] in code); [D] per-step cost scales with the number of slots N, not with pixels; the actor head outputs a Gaussian (μ, σ)

name: Oasis
tagline: Open per-frame Minecraft DiT, space-time attention
summary: An early playable real-time diffusion world model (Minecraft), released with open weights ('Oasis 500M'). A ViT autoencoder maps each 360x640 frame to an 18x32x16 latent, which the DiT patchifies into 144 tokens; the DiT generates one frame at a time with full spatial attention inside the frame and causal temporal attention over a 32-frame window, trained with Diffusion Forcing. With context keys and values cached, each pass adds only 144 new tokens, so batch-1 serving is bound by weight reads rather than by FLOPs (the open reference loop has no cache); Decart's custom kernels and multi-GPU engine behind the 20 fps demo are closed.
facts: ViT-L/20 KL-VAE: 360x640 frame → 18x32 latent with 16 channels, no temporal compression; DiT patch 2 → 144 tokens per frame [D]
DiT-S/2 (open-oasis): 16 blocks, d 1024, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4; each block = spatial attention + MLP, then temporal attention + MLP, each pair with its own adaLN; no pretrained video base named
Factorized: full (bidirectional) spatial attention over the 144 tokens of a frame; causal temporal axial attention per spatial position over up to 32 frames; axial RoPE in space, RoPE in time

25-dim action vector per frame (23 binary key/button flags, several can be on at once, plus 2 continuous camera axes in [−1, 1]) → Linear(25, 1024), added to the timestep embedding that drives the adaLN modulations

Diffusion Forcing (independent noise level per frame), v-prediction, sigmoid beta schedule; reference sampler DDIM with 10 steps per frame, context frames held at noise level 14; the demo's step count is not disclosed
ViT-L/20 decoder (12 layers, width 1024) → 360x640 frame, once per generated frame

Sliding window of 32 frames; no KV cache in the reference loop, so every DDIM step re-runs the whole window (up to 32 × 144 = 4,608 tokens [D]); generated latents join the window directly, with no decode and re-encode; blog lists limited long-horizon memory as a known failure

360p at 20 fps, 47 ms per frame, on NVIDIA H100s (company claim; GPUs per stream and demo checkpoint size not disclosed); the open 500M model runs at 2.58 FPS in MineWorld's Table 1 (third party, GPU not stated)

Per-frame generation with 144-token passes: ≈0.12 TFLOP per cached pass against ≈1.2 GB of 16-bit weights (≈608M params), so single-stream decoding is weight-bandwidth-bound and batching users is the lever [D]

name: JOWA
summary: An offline, multi-game world-action model: one GPT-2-style transformer over IRIS-like token sequences learns the world model (next observation tokens, reward, termination) and the Q-function at the same time, pretrained on 15 Atari games with 10M transitions each. At decision time a short beam search (horizon 2) over the model's own imagined futures corrects the Q-estimates. Beams are batched, but every imagined frame still costs 36 sequential token decodes, and planning drops throughput from 10.8 to 1.26 FPS.
tagline: One GPT for Atari dynamics and Q-values
facts: VQ-VAE on 84×84 grayscale frames: 36 tokens per frame (6×6 [D]), vocabulary 2048; 3-layer CNN with self-attention at resolutions 6 and 12 (IRIS code base), frozen after stage 1
GPT-2 (minGPT): JOWA-150M 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads; JOWA-70M 6 × 768 × 12; JOWA-40M 4 × 512 × 8; dropout 0.1; input = vocabulary + position + learnable task embedding
Causal over interleaved (z_t^1..z_t^36, a_t) tokens; L = 8 steps, max 296 tokens (8 × 37 [D])

One action token per step (18-action Atari space) plus a task embedding; the Q-head reads the output at the last observation token z_t^36 of each step, the reward and done heads the action token; next-code, reward and done heads are 2-layer MLPs; the JOWA-150M Q-head is a 3-layer MLP (hidden 1,792, 3 distributional heads; 40M and 70M: 1 head, hidden 768 and 1,024) trained by TD with CQL

Next observation token autoregressive within a frame, z_t^k | z_≤t-1, z_t^<k, a_≤t-1, so 36 serial decodes per imagined frame [D]; reward sign {-1, 0, 1} and termination as classification; distributional Q-head (3-layer MLP, hidden 1792, 3 heads for 150M) trained by TD learning

VQ-VAE CNN decoder; decisions use only token-space heads, but the released code decodes every imagined frame during beam search (K + K² frames per action, output discarded) and turns decoded imagined frames into synthetic fine-tuning data

Context up to 8 steps = 296 tokens; with planning at most 8 − H = 6 real steps plus 2 imagined. The paper gives no cache details; the released code keeps a per-layer KV cache (prefill once, then single-token cached passes; per-beam caches concatenated for batched beam search)

JOWA-150M on 7 games: 10.8 FPS without planning, 1.26 FPS with beam search (H = 2, K = 2-4), 0.12 FPS with MCTS; hardware not stated (authors, Table 5). Pretraining 1.75M steps, 'around 12 days on A100 GPUs', GPU count not given

Beam search calls the world model K²(H−1)+K times but takes only H forward latencies because beams are batched; at H = 2 the released code runs 1 prefill + 2 × 37 = 75 serial transformer passes per action [D]; 1.26 FPS ≈ 0.79 s per frame [D] (the paper does not say whether FPS counts decisions or emulator frames at frame skip 4)

name: Δ-IRIS
summary: IRIS with context-aware tokens. A CNN autoencoder conditioned on the previous frame and action encodes only the stochastic change between steps as 4 delta tokens from a 1,024-entry vocabulary, and a 3-layer GPT sees 6 tokens per step instead of IRIS's 17: one continuous I-token (a frame embedding from an auxiliary CNN), one action token and the 4 delta tokens. The Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) replaces the RSSM's GRU: the deterministic state h_t is a causal transformer over the past stochastic latents and actions, one token per step, and the posterior drops h_t so every step trains in parallel. name: Trajectory Transformer
summary: Offline RL as one big sequence-modeling problem: every state dimension, action dimension, the reward and the reward-to-go are discretized into 100 bins and become separate tokens of a small GPT. There is no learned encoder and no policy network; acting is beam search over the model's own trajectory predictions, extended one token at a time. Latency scales with state dimensionality, and the authors note it can take seconds per action, which, they say, precludes real-time control for most dynamical systems.
tagline: GPT over binned states, actions and rewards
facts: Each of the N state and M action dimensions, the reward and the reward-to-go is one token: per-dimension uniform or quantile discretization into V = 100 bins; input vocabulary V × (N + M + 2), output logits over V
GPT-style decoder: 4 layers, 4 heads, token embedding d 128, dropout 0.1; parameter count not disclosed (~12·4·128² ≈ 0.8M block weights if the MLP is 4× wide [D])

Causal, with every reward-to-go token masked out as a key (official code); context 5 transitions of (s, a, r, R), at most 5 × (N + M + 2) − 1 tokens, e.g. 124 for a 17-D state and 6-D action [D]; training uses 10-transition sequences (code)
Action dimensions are ordinary tokens in the stream, decoded after the state tokens of the same step

Next-token softmax, one token per pass, teacher-forced training; planning = beam search, horizon 15 transitions, observations decoded greedily (k_obs 1); paper (App. E): width 256, actions from the top 20 tokens; released code: 128 beams × 2 expansions, actions sampled after dropping the least likely tokens holding 60% of the mass (cdf_act 0.6); offline RL ranks transitions by reward plus reward-to-go instead of log-probability
None; states are discretized scalars, decoded back by bin centres
Fixed context of 5 transitions; no KV-cache details given
'Up to multiple seconds for action selection when the context window grows too large', hardware not stated (authors, Sec. 5); training 6-12 h per model on one V100 for 80 epochs (authors, App. A)

Per executed action: 15 × (N + M + 2) − N sequential single-token decodes (the current state is given and the last state is not sampled), e.g. 358 for HalfCheetah at horizon 15 [D]; code batches 256 rows for action and reward tokens, 128 for state tokens; a latency-bound ~1.5M-parameter workload [D]
